title: Part Z (Whole-Life Carbon) - Government Consultation
description: Part Z remains an industry-led proposal for whole-life carbon reporting, not a government consultation heading toward a mandate. In March 2026 the government rejected the Environmental Audit Committee's recommendation to mandate whole-life carbon assessments for major developments, opting for a voluntary approach. NISTA published a voluntary Whole Life Carbon Management Handbook (March 2026) instead of regulation.
impact: Major projects should voluntarily adopt whole-life carbon assessments using the NISTA handbook, as there is currently no mandate planned.

title: Building Safety Act - Principal Designer Registration Deadline
description: All Principal Designers and Principal Contractors for higher-risk buildings must be registered with the Building Safety Regulator (BSR).
impact: Failure to register means inability to work on HRBs. Check BSR registration status immediately.

title: Heat Network Zoning (England) - Government Response Published
description: In January 2026 the government published its formal response to the 2023 heat network zoning consultation, setting out implementation in England under Energy Act 2023 powers. These include powers to require certain buildings to connect, appoint zone developers, and designate zones. Zone designation and implementation will follow.
impact: Developers and contractors should assess whether projects fall within likely designated zones and plan for potential mandatory heat network connection.

title: UK Net Zero Carbon Building Standard (UKNZCBS) - Published
description: UKNZCBS published covering both embodied and operational emissions. Sets verified performance targets for new residential, commercial, and education buildings across energy use intensity, embodied carbon, and airtightness.
impact: Defines what 'net zero carbon' means for UK buildings. Voluntary but rapidly becoming market expectation for major developers.

title: FCA CP26/5 - Sustainability Disclosures Consultation (Closed)
description: The FCA consulted (30 January to 20 March 2026) on requiring listed issuers to disclose against the UK SRS, replacing current climate disclosure rules. The outcome has now been published as policy statement PS26/19 (30 September 2026), finalising comply-or-explain rules applying to accounting periods from 1 January 2027 with first reporting in 2028.
impact: Listed construction companies should prepare to disclose against UK SRS and build Scope 3 supply-chain data systems ahead of the 1 January 2027 start.

title: UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (UK SRS S1 & S2) - Final Standards Published
description: The Department for Business and Trade published the final UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (UK SRS S1 and S2) on 25 February 2026, based on the ISSB standards with six minor UK amendments. These provide the definitive basis for voluntary adoption ahead of expected mandatory requirements.
impact: Companies should align their sustainability reporting frameworks and Scope 3 data collection with the final UK SRS S1 and S2 standards now.

title: UK Sustainability Reporting Standards - Voluntary Adoption
description: UK SRS (based on ISSB standards) now available for voluntary adoption. Companies can begin reporting ahead of mandatory requirements expected in 2027.
impact: Early adopters gain competitive advantage with investors and clients. Scope 3 reporting preparation essential for supply chain.

title: Future Homes & Buildings Standards - Published
description: Government has laid the regulations for the Future Homes Standard and Future Buildings Standard via SI 2026/335 (The Building Regulations etc. (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2026), publishing updated Approved Documents L and F (2026). New homes must be built with solar panels, low-carbon heating (heat pumps/heat networks), and high fabric efficiency as standard, achieving at least 75% less carbon than 2013 standards. Compliance is initially demonstrated using SAP 10.3; the Home Energy Model (HEM) is not yet an approved methodology and is expected to follow later. Regulations come into force 24 March 2027 (24 September 2027 for higher-risk building work), subject to transitional provisions.
impact: Housebuilders must prepare supply chains for heat pumps, solar PV, and MVHR, and upskill for SAP 10.3 compliance now, with HEM adoption to follow.

title: Future Buildings Standard - Published
description: Published alongside the Future Homes Standard under SI 2026/335. Sets new energy performance requirements for non-domestic buildings including updated Parts L and F. Compliance is initially demonstrated using SAP 10.3 rather than the Home Energy Model. Regulations come into force 24 March 2027 (24 September 2027 for higher-risk building work), subject to transitional provisions.
impact: Commercial developers must prepare for updated compliance requirements using SAP 10.3, with new non-domestic buildings needing significantly higher energy performance.

title: Biodiversity Net Gain - Small Sites Compliance
description: SI 2026/790 (in force 6 August 2026), following the April 2026 government response, introduced a 0.2 hectare exemption so the smallest developments are no longer required to deliver mandatory BNG (unless on-site priority habitat is harmed). It also added a temporary-development exemption, a modified gain hierarchy for minor sites, and removed the self/custom-build exemption. Other developments still deliver minimum 10% BNG.
impact: Developers should check whether sites fall under the 0.2ha exemption; larger sites must still factor in 10% BNG costs and land requirements.

title: UK SRS - Mandatory FCA Rules Expected
description: FCA published policy statement PS26/19 on 30 September 2026 finalising sustainability disclosure rules for listed issuers against UK SRS. Rules are comply-or-explain (not strictly mandatory) and apply to accounting periods starting on or after 1 January 2027, with first reporting in 2028. Transitional reliefs apply: 1 year for Scope 3 and 2 years for wider UK SRS S1 disclosures.
impact: Listed construction companies should build Scope 3 supply-chain data systems now to report against UK SRS for accounting periods from 1 January 2027.

title: UK CBAM - Importer Registration Opens
description: Importers of aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, and iron & steel must register ahead of the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism launch in January 2027. Ceramics and glass are excluded from 2027. A minimum registration threshold of £50,000 of relevant imports applies.
impact: Importers should assess whether they exceed the £50,000 threshold across the five in-scope sectors, understand supply-chain carbon content, and prepare reporting systems.

title: UK CBAM - Full Launch
description: UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism launches, applying a carbon levy to imports across five sectors: aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, and iron & steel. Ceramics, glass, and electricity are not in scope for 2027. Based on actual or default emission values; indirect emissions delayed to 2029 at the earliest.
impact: Imported in-scope construction materials face carbon pricing; UK domestic manufacturers may gain advantage and imported steel/aluminium costs likely rise.

title: Future Homes Standard - Transitional Arrangements
description: Transitional provisions under SI 2026/335 allowing approved plans to proceed under current Part L before full FHS takes effect. For transitional protection, notices must be submitted before 24 March 2027 and construction commenced within the transitional window (by around 24 March 2028). SME developers get no blanket exemption.
impact: Window closing for developers - submit building notices before 24 March 2027 and commence work by ~24 March 2028 to retain transitional protection.

title: EPC Reform - New Energy Performance Metrics
description: EPCs move from a single headline rating to four metrics (energy cost, fabric performance, heating system, smart readiness) calculated with the Home Energy Model. Partial government response published 21 January 2026; launch was delayed in March 2026 from October 2026 to the second half of 2027, with the exact date due to be agreed by summer 2026.
impact: Landlords, developers and assessors should plan for the four-metric EPC regime and HEM-based assessments arriving during 2027.

title: Part Z - Mandatory Embodied Carbon Limits (Expected)
description: Possible future introduction of mandatory whole-life carbon reporting and embodied carbon limits for buildings over 1,000m2, which would require A1-A5 reporting at planning stage and whole-life (A-C) at completion. This is speculative and not government policy: in March 2026 the government opted for a voluntary approach to whole-life carbon rather than regulation.
impact: Developers and designers should treat low-carbon specification and material passports as best practice, while noting no mandate is currently planned.

title: Future Homes Standard - Full Compliance Required
description: All new homes must meet the full Future Homes Standard after the transitional period ends (~24 March 2028, roughly 12 months after the regulations come into force on 24 March 2027 under SI 2026/335). Solar panels, low-carbon heating (heat pumps or heat networks), and high fabric efficiency mandatory. No new gas boilers. At least 75% less carbon emissions than 2013 standards. Compliance demonstrated via SAP 10.3 (HEM to follow later).
impact: Every new home must have solar, a heat pump, and meet stringent fabric standards; housebuilders must adapt supply chains and designs before the transitional tail ends around March 2028.

title: UK SRS - First Mandatory Reports Due
description: First reports under the FCA's UK SRS regime (PS26/19) fall due in 2028, covering accounting periods starting on or after 1 January 2027. Rules are comply-or-explain. Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions reporting required, with transitional reliefs for Scope 3 and wider S1 disclosures.
impact: Construction companies must have emissions data systems in place by 2028; supply chain data requests will cascade to subcontractors and manufacturers.

title: EPC Rating C - Domestic Rented Properties (Proposed)
description: Government response published 21 January 2026 confirming privately rented homes in England and Wales must meet the equivalent of EPC C by a single compliance date of 1 October 2030. A dual-metric standard applies (fabric performance first, then a heating-system or smart-readiness standard), with a raised cost cap of £10,000 and 10-year exemption validity. Legislation to follow, with a statutory instrument aimed to come into force in 2027.
impact: Landlords should plan retrofits now to meet EPC C by 1 October 2030, budgeting up to the £10,000 cost cap and prioritising fabric-first improvements.

title: EPC Rating C Minimum - Non-Domestic (Proposed)
description: The 2027 interim EPC C milestone for non-domestic private-rented buildings has been scrapped (Written Ministerial Statement HCWS126, 18 June 2026). Instead, from 2031 non-domestic private-rented buildings over 1,000m2 in England and Wales must meet EPC B where cost-effective. Buildings under 1,000m2 remain at the current EPC E minimum.
impact: Landlords of non-domestic buildings over 1,000m2 should plan retrofits to reach EPC B by 2031; smaller buildings stay at EPC E.
